findings: F1 (PASS): transparency repo cold-restore RTO 0.43s, RPO 0 (push-on-write doctrine), verified against anchor bindings 3/3.
F2 (PASS): external immutable surface (Zenodo) reachable and live - the out-of-band anchor for maximal-attacker detection survives local loss by construction.

F3 (GAP, disclosed): hub entity layer has NO byte-exact backup surface - LEDGER.md and DAY_RECEIPTS carry structural summaries (RPO: since last receipt), raw entity payloads are not exportable from this session type. Candidate: scheduled entity-export snapshots committed to the transparency repo.

F4 (GAP, disclosed, owner decision): signing keys (.gov_release_key, .gov_ed25519_key, .issuance_key) are process-bound, gitignored by design, no escrow. Loss recovery = rotation cycle (new keypair + git-anchored re-pin + human GO), which is legitimate but leaves a signing gap window. Escrow policy (encrypted shards, owner custody) is an owner decision gate - surfaced, not decided.

F5 (CONTEXT): the Hub has survived one real disaster already (frontend loss to GitHub history-rewrite sync, rebuilt per hub-recovery note); this drill is the first FORMAL DR receipt. The old BackupStatus record (qe-001, Sept 1) was stale; superseded by 4 live-surface records.
